scope: Supplied raise/3 trace preparation and terminal BIF execution. Native error/exit/throw classes, badarg return, uncaught-throw promotion and monitor reasons are admitted. Catch/unwind and build_stacktrace instructions remain unadmitted.
adaptations: raise_trace.c adapts raise_3 syntax and normalization. Invalid classes, frames, locations and improper outer lists return a BADARG classification, not a raised exception. As upstream, Args/Arity values and location-list contents are not validated more strictly.

All frames are checked, including the suffix beyond DEFAULT_BACKTRACE_SIZE=8. The retained prefix is always copied; two-element fun frames gain a NIL location and legacy MFA triples become four-tuples. This removes only the native no-copy optimization, not observable values.

bif_exception.c publishes fvalue/ftrace/freason only after successful preparation; invalid syntax returns am_badarg. ftrace is a moving process root and participates in alias scanning and GC charging. Terminal uncaught throws become {nocatch,Value} errors; a supplied trace retains its original class payload while the terminal exception class is promoted. stacktrace.c uses the supplied symbolic frames rather than recapturing the current stack for monitor errors.

The native opaque {NegativeBignum,SymbolicTrace,NIL} representation retains the five-word 64-bit StackTrace prefix. Its supplied-trace marker has zero PC/current/depth/max_depth, so there are no hidden code roots. The negative-bignum payload preserves class and primary flags without SAVETRACE.

Input rooting uses the existing construction_root through fallible GC; allocation reserves in addition to outstanding heap credit. Publication occurs only after all fallible work. Pending exception state and output remain unchanged on failure. Work charges cover every inspected frame, retained construction and bulk heap writes; moving GC uses its existing ledger.

core_raise_trace_test covers full-suffix syntax rejection, normalization/truncation, exact supplied-trace layout, real moving GC, unchanged pending exceptions, separate memory-limit/OOM outcomes and every work-credit boundary through exact success. raise_trace_reference.erl independently establishes representative values on installed OTP 28.4.1; that reference VM is not used for libbeam execution. core_raise_execution_test additionally exercises compiled raise/3 with all classes, malformed arguments, fun frames, trace-only GC roots and supplied monitor reasons. core_raise_work_test uses the actual shared worker and exact/one-below budgets, peer survival, private-world reuse and monitored-child trace propagation. Handler integration remains pending.
